title: TSMC September Revenue Jumps 54.6% as Growth Continues
gist: TSMC reported September 2026 revenue of NT$511.86 billion, up 54.6% year on year and down 0.6% from August, with January-September revenue of NT$3.90 trillion up 41.1%. The release gives no customer, node, capex or AI-specific breakdown.

insights.claim: TSMC's September 2026 consolidated revenue was NT$511.86 billion, up 54.6% from a year earlier, though slightly lower than August.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Confirms very strong annual growth at the leading foundry.
insights.quote: TSMC reported September 2026 consolidated revenue of NT$511.86 billion, up 54.6% from a year earlier

insights.claim: September revenue fell 0.6% from August's NT$514.81 billion, while exceeding September 2025's NT$330.98 billion by about NT$180.88 billion.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A small monthly dip should be read against the large annual trend.

insights.claim: TSMC's January-September 2026 revenue was NT$3.90 trillion, up 41.1% on the same period of 2025, indicating sustained expansion rather than an isolated spike.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Nine-month growth shows the run-rate is broad-based across the year.

themes.theme: What the data does and does not show

insights.claim: TSMC's revenue is a useful indicator of semiconductor supply chain activity, relevant to suppliers of fabrication equipment, materials and supporting services.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Foundry sales growth is a read-through for upstream equipment and materials vendors.

insights.claim: Sustained sales growth can strengthen the financial foundation for capacity additions and technology development, but this release contains no capital expenditure update, capacity figures or process node breakdown.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Capex direction cannot be inferred from the monthly revenue report alone.
insights.locator: The scale of growth also matters

insights.claim: The monthly report does not separate AI processors from smartphone, automotive or other chips, nor disclose unit shipments, pricing, profitability or customer concentration, so it does not prove AI-specific demand growth.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Attributing the revenue surge to AI demand requires other disclosures such as earnings.
